title: Steve Jobs on building insanely great products and keeping Apple's spirit (Playboy interview, 1985)
summary: In this 1985 Playboy interview, Jobs explains why the Mac team built the computer for themselves, why craft must run all the way through a product, and why big companies lose great people to middle management. He also owns up to the Lisa and Apple III failures and describes making technology radically easier to use.

principles.text: Build the product for yourself and let your own taste judge it, not market research.
principles.quote: We built it for ourselves. We were the group of people who were going to judge whether it was great or not. We weren't going to go out and do market research.

principles.text: Carry quality through to the parts nobody sees, because you know it is there.
principles.quote: When you're a carpenter making a beautiful chest of drawers, you're not going to use a piece of plywood on the back, even though it faces the wall and nobody will ever see it.

principles.text: Growing companies lose their vision when layers of management separate leaders from the people doing the work.
principles.quote: Companies, as they grow to become multibillion-dollar entities, somehow lose their vision. They insert lots of layers of middle management between the people running the company and the people doing the work.

principles.text: Great people leave when individual accomplishment is discouraged, and mediocrity is what remains.
principles.quote: you don't keep great people under working environments where individual accomplishment is discouraged rather than encouraged. The great people leave and you end up with mediocrity.

principles.text: Recruit people who want to take on big risk early and make a mark on the world.
principles.quote: Someone who really wants to get in a little over his head and make a little dent in the universe.

principles.text: To reach the mass market, make a clean break and make the product radically easier to use and more powerful.
principles.quote: we needed a technology that would make the thing radically easier to use and more powerful at the same time, so we had to make a break.
